title: Epstein circle's gravity interest as an electrogravitics/UFO quest

tellings.quote: Therefore, I suspect that the interest in gravity is an interest in electrogravitics and you know the Townson Brown effect and basically it's all part of the UFO phenomenon that they're trying to crack.

tellings.page: section "“I wish I never met him.”", paragraph 10
tellings.quote: Jeffrey Epstein was also obsessed with physics research and technological developments directed toward defying gravity. In other words, he was interested in electrogravitics or what is believed to be the power and propulsion system of UFOs.

plain: Jeffrey Epstein's interest in defying gravity was really an attempt to crack the UFO question, according to the philosopher Jason Jorjani. On the show he puts it as a suspicion: the interest was in electrogravitics, the idea of using electricity to counter gravity, and in the effect named after Thomas Townsend Brown, all "part of the UFO phenomenon that they're trying to crack." In his own piece Ocean Outlaw: A Portrait of Ghislaine Maxwell, published in July 2025, he says it more firmly, writing that Epstein "was interested in electrogravitics or what is believed to be the power and propulsion system of UFOs", with the same tie to UFOs in both.

discussion.by: Ocean Outlaw: A Portrait of Ghislaine Maxwell
discussion.text: In the piece Jorjani states Epstein's interest in electrogravitics as a fact ("In other words, he was interested in electrogravitics or what is believed to be the power and propulsion system of UFOs"), where on the podcast he voices it as a suspicion; the tie to the UFO question is the same in both.
